To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Mott critical concentration nc is the electron concentration at the metal-insu-lator transition in a film of doped semiconductor nanoparticles devoid of ligands and in direct contact.
the Mott criterion can be applied to the films of doped nanocrystal and that the metal-insulator transitions in such films occurs for electron densities close to the Mott criterion.
the metal-insulator (MI) transition is achieved in films of ligand-free, doped silicon nanocrystals (Si NCs) at a critical carrier density (nc) of 2.5 × 1019 cm-3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic properties of doped semiconductor nanoparticles and films.
the development of new electronic materials based on films of doped nanocrystal semiconductors.
the metal-insulator transitions in films of damped nanocrystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metal-insulator transitions observed for the doped semiconductor nanoclusters in the experiments are consistent with the theoretical predictions.
the metal-insulator (MI) transition is a function of the number of electrons in the film, the nanocrystal diameter, and the dielectric constant of the medium.
the metal-insulator (M-I) transition is a function of the size of the nanocrystals and the dopant concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Mott criterion for the metal-insulator transitions in films of dopped semiconductor nanocrystals is the same as in bulk materials, and that it can be achieved with a relatively low doping concentration.
the critical concentration nc is a function of the film thickness.

, for films of doped nanocrystal, the Mott criterion should be modified by a factor 2.5 to account for the finite size of the nanocrystals and for the fact that the nanocrystals are in contact with each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the critical electron density required to induce a metal-like conduction in films of doted semiconductor nanocrystals is lower than the Mott criterion for bulk semiconducting materials, and it can be achieved at dopant concentrations as low as 0.1%.
the critical concentration of doped carriers for a metal-insulator transition in a semiconductor nanocrystal film is significantly higher than in bulk.
the metal-insulator threshold in doped semiconductor nanomaterials is determined by the nanocrystal volume rather than their surface area.
